title: No Kings movement and immigrant rights groups hold weekend rallies in Boise
seoTitle: Boise No Kings and immigration rallies

tea.why: Protesters gathered to encourage early voting, oppose the administration's agenda, and demand accountability for civil rights violations.
tea.want: Participants wanted to mobilize voters for the general election and end the inhumane treatment of immigrants in Idaho.
tea.changed: Oct 18: Demonstrators marched from Ann Morrison Park to the Idaho State Capitol to demand government accountability.

summary: Over the weekend, multiple rallies took place in Boise ahead of the upcoming general election. On Saturday, Oct. 17, the Idaho State Capitol hosted a No Kings protest organized by Idaho 50501 and local grassroots groups, aimed at encouraging voter registration and early voting while addressing policies on Social Security, Medicare, immigration, and women's rights. On Sunday, Oct. 18, a second march led by organizations including PODER of Idaho, ACLU of Idaho, the Idaho Organization of Resource Councils, the Defend Immigrant Families Coalition, and Idaho 50501 traveled from Ann Morrison Park to the Idaho State Capitol. This second event marked the anniversary of a past immigration raid in Wilder and featured a petition demanding government accountability for civil rights violations, which organizers intended to deliver to Governor Brad Little.

updates.text: A No Kings protest was held at the Idaho State Capitol to encourage voter registration and turnout.
A second rally and march from Ann Morrison Park to the Capitol demanded accountability for past immigration raids.
